en.title: I Surrender All
en.author: Judson W. Van DeVenter
stanzas:
[D]All to Jesus [G]I sur[D]render,
All to [A7]Him I freely [D]give;
[D]I will ever [G]love and [D]trust Him,
In His [A7]presence daily [D]live.

All to Jesus I surrender,
Humbly at His feet I bow;
Worldly pleasures all forsaken,
Take me, Jesus, take me now.

All to Jesus I surrender,
Make me, Savior, wholly Thine;
Let me feel the Holy Spirit,
Truly know that Thou art mine.

All to Jesus I surrender,
Lord, I give myself to Thee;
Fill me with Thy love and power,
Let Thy blessing fall on me.

All to Jesus I surrender,
Now I feel the sacred flame;
Oh, the joy of full salvation!
Glory, glory, to His Name!
en.chorus:
[D]I surrender all,
[A7]I surrender [D]all;
[D]All to Thee, my [G]blessed [D]Savior,
I sur[A7]render [D]all.

notes: All five of Van DeVenter's stanzas, from Timeless Truths. Hymnary's representative text (Baptist Hymnal 1991) prints only stanzas 1, 3 and 4 of these, and hymnary's own note says the hymn "originally had five stanzas, but the last is usually omitted" — stanza 5 ("Now I feel the sacred flame") is the one most often dropped, and stanza 2 ("Humbly at His feet I bow") is frequently dropped too. Variant in stanza 3: this source reads "Let me feel the Holy Spirit"; the Baptist Hymnal reads "Let me feel Thy Holy Spirit". Key D matches both hymnary's tune SURRENDER (Weeden) and the Timeless Truths score, so the chart is at printed pitch. Hymnary disambiguates the tune as "SURRENDER (Weeden)"; the tune name proper is SURRENDER. Independently cross-checked 2026-08-01: amazinghymns.com prints all five stanzas in this order, including "Now I feel the sacred flame", and both it and gccsatx.com read "Let me feel the Holy Spirit" — so three sources carry this file's reading. Both cross-check sites lowercase the divine pronouns; this file keeps the traditional capitalisation of its primary source. Re-verified 2026-08-02 against hymnal.net (no. 441), a five-stanza printing in the same order: it confirms the D major key and the chorus word-for-word, but reads "Let me feel Thy Holy Spirit" in stanza 3 — so the "Thy" variant is NOT confined to abridged three-stanza printings (an earlier version of this note claimed it was); the two readings simply coexist across full printings, and this file keeps "the Holy Spirit" with its primary source. hymnal.net's other deltas are punctuation only (stanza 2 "I bow,"/"forsaken;", stanza 5 "flame." and "Glory, glory to His name!").
